rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(continence|urology and bowel)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. This is a framework membership list, not a market share and not the whole buying picture. The larger part of this patch is bought in the community on prescription, through NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IX and the dispensing appliance contractors, a route with no NHS Supply Chain framework page at all; the Drug Tariff summary is where that route appears, and the page's Market intelligence section sizes the two populations separately. Being named on a framework is not evidence of volume, and being absent from one is not evidence of absence from the market.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. This is a framework membership list, not a market share and not the whole buying picture. The larger part of this patch is bought in the community on prescription, through NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IX and the dispensing appliance contractors, a route with no NHS Supply Chain framework page at all; the Drug Tariff summary is where that route appears, and the page's Market intelligence section sizes the two populations separately. Being named on a framework is not evidence of volume, and being absent from one is not evidence of absence from the market.
rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(continence|incontinen\w*|urinary catheters?|urethral catheters?|indwelling catheters?|intermittent catheters?|foley|suprapubic|catheterisation|catheterization|urinary drainage|drainage bags?|leg bags?|night bags?|catheter valves?|catheter maintenance|urine meters?|urine collection|urine bags?|penile sheaths?|urinary sheaths?|uridome|stomas?|ostomy|colostomy|ileostomy|urostomy|bowel management|bowel care|faecal management|fecal management|anal irrigation|trans[- ]?anal irrigation|rectal irrigation|bladder washout|bladder irrigation|pelvic floor|continence pads?|absorbent pads?|pads and garments|commodes?|enuresis|nocturia)\b/i and does not match /\b(blood collection|catheterisation lab|surgical mesh)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. No CPV family corroborates this speciality: not one matching notice in this data carries a CPV code specific to it, so none is claimed. A CPV code could never admit a notice on its own in any case, because a notice carrying a basket of them is filed under all and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IXB/IXC/IXB & IXC for the stated effective month, summarised. Prices are the reimbursement price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's.

localIntel.title: Disposable and Washable Continence Care: suppliers by lot
localIntel.fact: Four lots. Lot 1 pants and shaped pads: Abena, Attends, Essity, Forma-Care, Healthcare 25, Paul Hartmann, Ontex. Lot 2 other disposables: the Lot 1 seven plus Meditrade UK and Sharon Services. Lot 3 washables: Abena, Attends, Essity, Forma-Care, GBUK, iMEDicare, P&S Healthcare, Sharon Services. Lot 4 sensor technology: Abena and Ontex only. £335m ex VAT. Bids received per lot: 9, 14, 9 and 2.
localIntel.use: Which lots each competitor can sell on. This settles the launch brief's own four-versus-seven lot contradiction: the award record has four.

localIntel.title: SBS10525 (successor to SBS10015): Lot 5 continence products home delivery
localIntel.fact: Lot 5 is 'Continence Products Home Delivery Service' (5a adult/bariatric, 5b paediatric). Estimated framework value £500m ex VAT across all lots. Tender closed 27/03/2026. SBS10015, the route almost every current England home-delivery award uses, expires 31/12/2026.
localIntel.use: Decides which suppliers trusts and ICBs can directly award home-delivery contracts to from 2027.

localIntel.org: NHS Wales (Hywel Dda UHB board paper)
localIntel.title: All Wales continence products contract
localIntel.fact: The All Wales contract expired 31/05/2025. A 12-month direct award went to Ontex Healthcare UK Ltd on the HealthTrust Europe framework, 01/06/2025 to 31/05/2026, while a mini-competition ran for the long-term requirement. Hywel Dda's share is £988,043.42 ex VAT a year. The paper puts raw material cost increases at about 3.4%.
localIntel.use: Wales buys nationally too. Who won from June 2026 is not verified; a Sell2Wales award notice would settle it.

localIntel.title: Incontinence products: free after public health nurse assessment
localIntel.fact: HSE supplies incontinence products free of charge after assessment by the patient's public health nurse. The national storage and distribution tender (HSE 23739, €25m estimate, 2024) is on eTenders; who won it is not verified.
localIntel.use: The Republic of Ireland route is PHN-assessed, not prescribed.

localIntel.title: Continence pads provision consultation
localIntel.fact: Spend on continence pads was about £2.1m against a budget of about £1.3m. Proposals: stop supplying lower-absorbency pads such as TENA Comfort Mini Super, move to a 16-week delivery cycle, and cut four pads to three per 24 hours.
localIntel.quote: readily available online and in a variety of stores
localIntel.use: Primary evidence that NHS rationing is pushing light incontinence into private pay.
